column1: # DEFECTS FOUND IN THE SOURCE SKILLS while distilling them into Gaia.
# Distillation reads source material closely enough to find things a normal reader would not,
# and those findings are worth more than the distilled prose. They are recorded here rather
# than silently corrected in Gaia, so that anyone still using the source can see them -- and so
# that Gaia's own version can be checked against a stated original.
# Verified by the wave lead, not taken on the finder's word.
2-D explicit diffusion bound stated as the 1-D one
column4: The von Neumann limit for explicit diffusion is Δx²/(2·D) in ONE dimension and Δx²/(4·D) in TWO. The prose permits a timestep twice the stable one for a 2-D grid.
column5: The same chapter's own pseudocode at :114 uses "0.25 cellSize² / max(D)" -- the correct 2-D form -- and reference-impl/glacier.py:85 ships "0.2 * cellsize² / dmax", correct and conservative. So the prose disagrees with both the pseudocode beside it and the code it describes.
column6: confirmed; Gaia carries the correct general form in simulation-time-budget.md

column1: the lmax depth ramp on transport capacity is attributed to Stava et al. 2008 across this field, including by Gaia's own first draft
column2: gaia/references/hydraulic-erosion.md sources, and the stava2008 bibliography note
column3: capacity ramped by lmax(d1) cited to [stava2008]
column4: Stava's capacity (eq. 2) is |v|*C_k*sin(alpha), UNRAMPED -- the string `lmax` does not occur in the paper. The ramp is Jako & Toth 2011 eq. (10), lmax(x) = 0 below zero depth, linear, 1 at Kdmax.
column5: PDFs of both papers were fetched and their text extracted; eq. (10) was read in Jako's CESCG 2011 printing (old.cescg.org). The stava2008 entry now states explicitly that it does NOT contain the ramp, so the correction survives in the place a reader checks.
column6: corrected; jako2011 added, and its locator names the CESCG printing because that is the copy whose equation numbering was read

column1: the virtual-pipe model is described as having a depth-dependent signal speed, which is false for the constant cross-section every source actually specifies
column3: celerity rises with depth, so a filling pool gets progressively more expensive; recompute the limit from the current state every step
column4: Mei eq. (2) gives A as a pipe cross-section parameter with no depth dependence, and Stava sec. 4 eq. (1) is decisive: "In our simulation this area is always constant with profile C = l^2". Linearising gives signal speed sqrt(g*A/l) -- an EFFECTIVE depth set by A/l, not the water depth. With Stava's A = l^2 the grid sloshes like water one cell deep no matter how deep the pool is.
column5: Bisected critical dt with the clamp disabled: constant A=1 gives dt_crit 0.1604 at depths 0.1, 1.0 and 10 alike; A = h*lx gives 0.5056 / 0.1599 / 0.0506. The ratio dt_crit/(dx/sqrt(g*A/l)) held at 0.502 across A in {1,4}, l in {1,4}, dx in {1,2} and two decades of depth. Advective speed is not in the constant-A bound either: dt_crit moved only 0.1604 -> 0.1601 as background transport went 0 -> 50 m/s.
column6: corrected; the document now says which bound governs which formulation rather than printing one bound for both

column1: Zevenbergen & Thorne's equation numbering could not be verified, and the locator was deliberately NOT sharpened
column3: the locator is a topic paraphrase, and stays one
column4: Nothing is known to be wrong. The paper is paywalled, and the reproductions checked (RichDEM docs, RSAGA wiki, SAGA forums, an arXiv roughness paper) give the method without numbered equations.
column5: The coefficients themselves were NOT taken from memory: the 9-point partial-quartic interpolation was solved exactly in rationals (Vandermonde inverse over Fraction) and read off, then checked -- exact to 12 digits on a quadratic surface, second-order convergence on a Gaussian hill (error ratios 4.00/4.00/4.00 per halving of L), plan/sqrt(p) reproducing a contour's 1/r to 7 digits, and the ridge/valley sign convention confirmed. So the MATH is verified while the LOCATOR is not, and those are different claims.
column6: OPEN -- writing "eq. 15" from memory would be a `?` wearing a P's confidence, so the paraphrase stands until someone reads the paper
